description: Add the House Bot cheating/lying mode (Task 11.2 / REQ-17.2) and bot labelling in the room (REQ-17.3), with a test that demonstrates the lie is CAUGHT via the finalisation path. Depends on FEAT-001 (the honest bot and package scaffold).
steps: Cheating seam (shared code path). The protocol Session (packages/protocol/src/session.ts) auto-answers HONESTLY in its private step() via `score(s.secret, d.guesses[index])` and has no hook to send a different ANSWER. To let the cheating bot run through the EXACT SAME Session code path as the honest bot (REQ-17.1 'same code paths'), add a minimal, backward-compatible optional seam to Session: an optional config field such as `answerPolicy?: (ctx: { index: number; guess: Code; secret: Code; honest: Feedback }) => Feedback`. In step(), compute the honest feedback with score() as today, then if an answerPolicy is provided pass it through the policy and use its return value as the ANSWER feedback; otherwise use the honest value unchanged. The returned feedback must still be a valid Feedback (the ANSWER encoder already enforces isValidFeedback). This is the ONLY change to session.ts and MUST be additive: existing Session.create callers (web controller, protocol tests) behave identically when answerPolicy is undefined. Thread the field through SessionConfig and the private constructor/create. Keep the type imports as `import type` to satisfy verbatimModuleSyntax.

Add corresponding protocol tests if coverage requires it: a session-level test in packages/protocol confirming that with answerPolicy returning a wrong feedback for one index, the resulting transcript carries the lie and finalise() charges a 'wrong-answer' fault to the lying seat and awards the win to the other seat by reason 'fault'. (If existing REQ-18.3 lying-answer coverage already exercises findLies, keep this test focused on the new seam specifically.) Ensure packages/protocol coverage thresholds still pass.

In apps/house-bot/src/bot.ts, add a cheating configuration to HouseBot. Accept an optional `cheat` option, e.g. `cheat?: { atGuessIndex: number }` or `cheat?: { lieOnce: boolean }`. When cheating is enabled, construct the Session with an answerPolicy that, for the targeted answer index, returns a feedback DIFFERENT from the honest score (and still a valid Feedback value, e.g. pick any VALID_FEEDBACK value not equal to the honest one; never fabricate an invalid feedback since the encoder would reject it). For every other index it returns the honest feedback. Honest mode (no cheat option) passes no answerPolicy, so it is byte-for-byte the honest path from FEAT-001.

Bot labelling (REQ-17.3). Make the House Bot identifiable as a bot in the room. The relay HELLO payload is constrained to 'host'|'guest' and cannot carry a label, so add an explicit, documented label mechanism at the bot layer: expose a readonly `label` on HouseBot (default like 'House Bot') and a static/exported constant (e.g. HOUSE_BOT_LABEL). Provide a way for a room/opponent to learn it: EITHER (a) a small, documented out-of-band identity announcement the bot broadcasts/returns, OR (b) a clearly exported marker (constant + the bot's public key accessor) that a room UI uses to render the 'bot' badge, with a comment pointing at REQ-17.3. Pick the lightest option that is genuinely testable; do not weaken protocol message validation to carry it. Document the chosen mechanism in findings.

Create apps/house-bot/test/cheating.test.ts: set up the SAME two-bot harness as FEAT-001 (shared MemoryHub, shared MemoryChain, per-bot MemoryStorage, shared ManualClock, deterministic secrets + seeded rng), but make ONE bot a cheater that lies on a specific answer index while the other plays honestly. Advance the clock / settle / confirmAll so the game reaches 'final'. Assert: the honest bot's verdict is kind 'final' with reason 'fault', the result awards the win to the honest bot's seat, and verdict.faults contains a { seat: <cheater seat>, kind: 'wrong-answer', index, claimed, actual } entry where claimed !== actual. This demonstrates the lie is caught by finalisation (the design.md section 5 / REQ-18.3 lying-answer check), satisfying Task 11.2.
Add a test asserting the bot labelling: HouseBot exposes the bot label (e.g. equals HOUSE_BOT_LABEL / 'House Bot') and whatever room-facing marker was chosen, confirming REQ-17.3 is observable.
acceptance_criteria: A HouseBot can be configured to cheat and will send one ANSWER whose feedback differs from the true score while remaining a syntactically valid Feedback.

In the two-bot cheating test, the honest bot's final Verdict has kind 'final', reason 'fault', the win goes to the honest seat, and faults include a 'wrong-answer' fault charged to the cheater's seat with claimed !== actual.
The Session change is purely additive: with no answerPolicy, Session behaviour (and all existing protocol/web tests) is unchanged, and honest HouseBot play is identical to FEAT-001.
The House Bot is labelled as a bot in a way an opponent/room can observe (REQ-17.3), via an exported label/marker, without weakening protocol message validation.
Repo-root `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, and `pnpm test` all pass, and both apps/house-bot and packages/protocol coverage thresholds pass.
verification: Run `pnpm --filter @accident/house-bot test` and confirm the cheating-caught test and the labelling test pass.
Run `pnpm --filter @accident/protocol test` and confirm the new seam test and all existing protocol tests pass with coverage.
Run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, and `pnpm test` at repo root and confirm all pass.
